description: An examination of the meaning, natural and human causes, evidence, impacts, mitigation and adaptation measures of climate change with reference to Tanzania and Africa.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best defines climate change?

options.text: The day-to-day state of the atmosphere of a place
A long-term shift in average weather patterns and temperatures of an area over many years
A sudden thunderstorm that lasts only a few hours
The seasonal change from the wet season to the dry season

mcq.explanation: Climate change refers to long-term alterations in the average weather conditions (especially temperature and rainfall) of a place or the whole Earth over decades or longer, not short-term events.

mcq.questionText: The condition of the atmosphere of a particular place at a particular time is known as:

options.text: Climate
Season
Weather
Greenhouse effect

mcq.explanation: Weather is the day-to-day, short-term condition of the atmosphere, while climate is the average weather of an area over a long period (usually 30 years or more).

mcq.questionText: Which gas is the most significant contributor to the human-enhanced greenhouse effect?

options.text: Oxygen
Nitrogen
Carbon dioxide
Argon

mcq.explanation: Carbon dioxide, released mainly from burning fossil fuels and deforestation, is the largest single contributor to the enhanced greenhouse effect and global warming.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a clearly NATURAL cause of climate change?

options.text: Burning of coal and petrol
Volcanic eruptions releasing ash and gases
Industrial emissions from factories
Clearing forests for farming

mcq.explanation: Volcanic eruptions are a natural cause, releasing gases and ash that affect the climate. The other options are human (anthropogenic) causes.

mcq.questionText: The famous melting of ice on which Tanzanian mountain is often cited as evidence of climate change?

options.text: Mount Meru
Mount Kilimanjaro
The Uluguru Mountains
The Usambara Mountains

mcq.explanation: The retreat and melting of the ice cap and glaciers on Mount Kilimanjaro, the highest mountain in Africa, is widely used as visible evidence of global warming.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a major greenhouse gas produced largely by livestock, rice paddies and decaying waste?

options.text: Methane
Ozone at ground level only
Hydrogen
Helium

mcq.explanation: Methane (CH4) is a powerful greenhouse gas released from livestock digestion, flooded rice fields, and decomposing organic waste in landfills.

options.text: The cooling of the upper atmosphere
The gradual increase in the average temperature of the Earth's surface and atmosphere
A single very hot day during the dry season
The warming of ocean water during El Nino only

mcq.explanation: Global warming is the long-term rise in the Earth's average surface temperature, mainly caused by increasing concentrations of greenhouse gases.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a mitigation measure for climate change?

options.text: Building higher sea walls to keep out the rising sea
Switching to renewable energy such as solar and wind to cut emissions
Planting drought-resistant crop varieties
Moving settlements away from flood-prone areas

mcq.explanation: Mitigation aims to reduce the causes of climate change, for example by reducing greenhouse gas emissions through renewable energy. The other options are adaptation measures that help people cope with effects already happening.

mcq.questionText: The international agreement adopted in 2015 in which countries pledged to limit global warming to well below 2 degrees Celsius is the:

options.text: Paris Agreement
Berlin Wall Treaty
Arusha Declaration
Lagos Plan of Action

mcq.explanation: The Paris Agreement (2015) is the international treaty under which countries committed to limiting the global temperature rise to well below 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels.

mcq.questionText: Planting trees on a large scale to absorb carbon dioxide and combat climate change is called:

options.text: Deforestation
Desertification
Afforestation
Irrigation

mcq.explanation: Afforestation is the planting of trees in areas to create forests; trees absorb carbon dioxide through photosynthesis, helping to reduce greenhouse gases.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is the BEST example of how climate change threatens agriculture in Tanzania?

options.text: Increased number of mobile phones in rural areas
More reliable rainfall and bumper harvests every year
Unreliable rainfall and prolonged droughts reducing crop yields
Faster growth of urban industries

mcq.explanation: Tanzanian farming is largely rain-fed, so unreliable rainfall and prolonged droughts caused by climate change reduce crop yields and threaten food security.

mcq.questionText: The greenhouse effect is best described as:

options.text: The trapping of the Sun's heat in the atmosphere by certain gases
The reflection of all sunlight back into space
The growing of vegetables inside glass houses
The cooling effect of clouds at night

mcq.explanation: The greenhouse effect occurs when gases such as carbon dioxide and methane trap outgoing heat (long-wave radiation) in the atmosphere, keeping the Earth warm; an enhanced greenhouse effect causes global warming.

mcq.questionText: Rising sea levels caused by climate change are a particular threat to which type of area?

options.text: High mountain regions far inland
Low-lying coastal areas and islands such as Zanzibar and Dar es Salaam
Dry interior plateaus
Deep underground mines

mcq.explanation: Low-lying coastal areas and islands such as the Zanzibar islands and the Dar es Salaam coast are vulnerable to flooding, erosion and saltwater intrusion from rising sea levels.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following pairs correctly matches a measure with its category?

options.text: Using energy-efficient cookstoves to cut fuelwood use — mitigation
Burning more coal for electricity — adaptation
Cutting down forests for charcoal — mitigation
Releasing more methane from landfills — adaptation

mcq.explanation: Using energy-efficient cookstoves reduces fuelwood demand and emissions, so it is a mitigation measure. The other options either increase emissions or are wrongly categorised.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes weather variability from long-term climate change?

options.text: Weather variability lasts for thousands of years; climate change lasts a few hours
Weather variability is short-term day-to-day or seasonal change, while climate change is a sustained shift in averages over decades
They mean exactly the same thing
Weather variability only happens in Africa, climate change only in Europe

mcq.explanation: Weather variability refers to normal short-term fluctuations from day to day or season to season, while climate change is a long-term, sustained change in the average conditions over many decades.

fib.questionText: The average atmospheric conditions of a place recorded over a long period, usually 30 years or more, is called _____.
fib.explanation: Climate is the long-term average of weather elements such as temperature and rainfall for a place over at least 30 years.

fib.questionText: The gradual rise in the Earth's average surface temperature due to increasing greenhouse gases is known as global _____.
fib.explanation: Global warming is the long-term increase in the Earth's average temperature caused mainly by the enhanced greenhouse effect.

fib.questionText: The trapping of heat in the atmosphere by gases such as carbon dioxide and methane is called the _____ effect.
fib.explanation: The greenhouse effect describes how certain atmospheric gases trap outgoing heat, keeping the planet warm; its enhancement by human activity drives global warming.

fib.questionText: Large-scale planting of trees to absorb carbon dioxide and reduce climate change is called _____.
fib.explanation: Afforestation increases forest cover; trees act as carbon sinks by absorbing carbon dioxide during photosynthesis.

fib.questionText: The 2015 international treaty in which nations agreed to limit global temperature rise is known as the _____ Agreement.
fib.explanation: The Paris Agreement (2015) commits countries to limiting global warming to well below 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels.

fib.questionText: The greenhouse gas released mainly by livestock, flooded rice fields and decaying waste is _____.
fib.explanation: Methane (CH4) is a potent greenhouse gas produced by cattle digestion, rice paddies and the decomposition of organic waste.

fib.questionText: Measures taken to help people and ecosystems cope with the effects of climate change that are already happening are called _____ measures.
fib.explanation: Adaptation measures, such as drought-resistant crops and improved water storage, help communities adjust to climate change impacts, unlike mitigation which tackles the causes.

fib.questionText: The melting of the ice cap on Mount _____ in Tanzania is often given as visible evidence of climate change.
fib.explanation: The shrinking glaciers and ice cap on Mount Kilimanjaro, Africa's highest peak, are commonly cited as evidence of warming.

fib.questionText: Burning of fossil fuels such as coal, oil and natural gas is the main human source of the gas _____ in the atmosphere.
fib.explanation: Combustion of fossil fuels releases large amounts of carbon dioxide, the leading greenhouse gas driving global warming.

fib.questionText: Energy obtained from naturally replenished sources such as the sun and wind, which produces little or no greenhouse gas, is called _____ energy.
fib.explanation: Renewable energy sources such as solar and wind do not run out and emit little carbon dioxide, making them key to mitigating climate change.

tf.questionText: Weather refers to the short-term, day-to-day condition of the atmosphere of a place.
tf.explanation: Weather is the short-term state of the atmosphere, whereas climate is the long-term average over many years.

tf.questionText: Carbon dioxide and methane are examples of greenhouse gases.
tf.explanation: Both carbon dioxide and methane trap heat in the atmosphere and are major greenhouse gases.

tf.questionText: All causes of climate change are human-made; there are no natural causes.
tf.explanation: Climate change has both natural causes (such as volcanic eruptions and variations in the Sun's energy) and human causes (such as burning fossil fuels and deforestation).

tf.questionText: Deforestation increases climate change because it removes trees that would otherwise absorb carbon dioxide.
tf.explanation: Cutting down forests reduces the absorption of carbon dioxide and often releases stored carbon, worsening global warming.

tf.questionText: Rising sea levels pose no threat to coastal towns like Dar es Salaam.
tf.explanation: Rising sea levels threaten low-lying coastal areas such as Dar es Salaam and Zanzibar with flooding, erosion and saltwater intrusion.

tf.questionText: Mitigation measures aim to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, while adaptation measures help communities cope with impacts.
tf.explanation: Mitigation tackles the causes by cutting emissions, while adaptation helps people adjust to the effects that are already occurring.

tf.questionText: Climate change can increase the frequency of droughts and floods in Tanzania.
tf.explanation: A warming climate alters rainfall patterns, leading to more frequent and severe droughts and floods, which is evident in many parts of Tanzania and Africa.

tf.questionText: Switching from charcoal to solar energy for cooking and lighting helps reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
tf.explanation: Using clean, renewable solar energy instead of charcoal reduces both emissions and deforestation, supporting climate change mitigation.

tf.questionText: The Paris Agreement is a Tanzanian national law that applies only within Tanzania.
tf.explanation: The Paris Agreement is an international treaty involving many countries worldwide, not a national law of one country.

tf.questionText: Individuals can contribute to fighting climate change by planting trees, saving energy and reducing waste.
tf.explanation: Individual actions such as tree planting, conserving energy and reducing waste collectively help reduce greenhouse gas emissions and combat climate change.

summary.questionText: Briefly distinguish between weather and climate.
summary.correctAnswer: Weather is the short-term, day-to-day condition of the atmosphere of a place (such as temperature, rainfall and wind on a given day), while climate is the average of these atmospheric conditions over a long period, usually 30 years or more.
summary.explanation: The key difference is time scale: weather is short-term and changeable, climate is long-term and averaged.

summary.correctAnswer: Climate change is a long-term shift in the average weather patterns of a place or of the whole Earth, especially in temperature and rainfall, taking place over decades or longer.
summary.explanation: Climate change involves sustained changes in average conditions, distinct from normal short-term weather variability.

summary.questionText: State three human (anthropogenic) causes of climate change.
summary.correctAnswer: Burning of fossil fuels (coal, oil and gas) which releases carbon dioxide; deforestation which removes trees that absorb carbon dioxide; and industrial activities and agriculture (including livestock keeping) that release greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide and methane.
summary.explanation: Human activities increase greenhouse gas concentrations and reduce carbon sinks, driving global warming.

summary.questionText: Explain how the greenhouse effect leads to global warming.
summary.correctAnswer: The Sun's short-wave radiation reaches and warms the Earth, which then re-radiates heat as long-wave radiation. Greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide and methane absorb and trap this outgoing heat in the atmosphere. When human activity increases these gases, more heat is trapped, raising the Earth's average temperature, a process known as global warming.
summary.explanation: An enhanced greenhouse effect from extra greenhouse gases traps more heat, causing global warming.

summary.questionText: Give four pieces of evidence that show climate change is occurring.
summary.correctAnswer: Rising average global temperatures; melting glaciers and ice such as the shrinking ice cap on Mount Kilimanjaro; rising sea levels; and changing rainfall patterns with more frequent droughts and floods.
summary.explanation: These observable changes provide measurable evidence that the climate is warming and shifting.

summary.questionText: Describe two effects of climate change on agriculture in Tanzania.
summary.correctAnswer: Unreliable and reduced rainfall, together with prolonged droughts, lowers crop yields and threatens food security since most farming is rain-fed. Floods and changing seasons can also destroy crops, shift planting times and increase pests and diseases, reducing farmers' incomes.
summary.explanation: Tanzania's largely rain-fed agriculture is highly sensitive to changes in rainfall and temperature.

summary.questionText: Outline how climate change affects water resources and human health.
summary.correctAnswer: Climate change reduces water availability through droughts, shrinking rivers and lakes, and drying wells, while floods can contaminate water supplies. For health, it spreads diseases such as malaria and cholera into new areas, causes heat stress, and worsens malnutrition due to reduced food supplies.
summary.explanation: Water scarcity and disease spread are major impacts of climate change on communities.

summary.questionText: Distinguish between mitigation and adaptation measures, giving one example of each.
summary.correctAnswer: Mitigation measures aim to reduce the causes of climate change by cutting greenhouse gas emissions, for example using renewable solar energy instead of fossil fuels. Adaptation measures help people and ecosystems cope with impacts already happening, for example planting drought-resistant crops or building flood defences.
summary.explanation: Mitigation targets causes; adaptation targets coping with effects.

summary.questionText: Suggest four mitigation measures that can reduce climate change.
summary.correctAnswer: Reducing greenhouse gas emissions by using renewable energy such as solar, wind and hydro; afforestation and reforestation to absorb carbon dioxide; improving energy efficiency and using clean cookstoves; and reducing deforestation and proper waste management to cut methane.
summary.explanation: These measures lower emissions or increase carbon absorption, reducing the drivers of climate change.

summary.questionText: Explain the role of individuals and governments in combating climate change.
summary.correctAnswer: Individuals can plant trees, save energy, use clean fuels, reduce and recycle waste, and raise awareness. Governments can make and enforce environmental laws, promote renewable energy and afforestation programmes, educate the public, and participate in international efforts such as the Paris Agreement.
summary.explanation: Both personal action and national policy, alongside international cooperation, are needed to tackle climate change effectively.

hoq.questionText: A district in central Tanzania has experienced repeated crop failure due to prolonged droughts, and many families now face hunger. Which combination of measures would BEST help the community both cope now and reduce future contributions to climate change?

options.text: Plant drought-resistant crops and harvest rainwater while also switching to solar energy and planting trees
Cut down more forests to sell charcoal and buy food from the market
Wait for the rains to return and continue using the same farming methods
Move everyone permanently to the coast and abandon farming

hoq.explanation: Planting drought-resistant crops and harvesting rainwater are adaptation measures that help the community cope now, while switching to solar energy and planting trees are mitigation measures that reduce emissions and absorb carbon dioxide. The other options worsen the problem or are impractical.

hoq.questionText: Two students argue about Mount Kilimanjaro. Student A says the shrinking ice cap proves the climate is changing; Student B says one hot week last year is the real proof. Whose reasoning is geographically sound and why?

options.text: Student B, because a single hot week shows a long-term trend
Student A, because the long-term retreat of the ice cap reflects a sustained change in climate, while a single hot week is only short-term weather
Both are equally correct because weather and climate are the same
Neither, because ice never melts naturally

hoq.explanation: The decades-long retreat of Kilimanjaro's ice cap is evidence of long-term climate change, whereas one hot week is short-term weather variability and cannot by itself prove a change in climate.

hoq.questionText: An African country wants to expand electricity supply while honouring its Paris Agreement commitments. Which energy strategy is the most consistent with both goals?

options.text: Build several large coal-fired power stations because coal is cheap
Invest in hydro, solar and wind power, which generate electricity with little greenhouse gas emission
Import diesel generators for every village
Burn more firewood and charcoal in power plants

hoq.explanation: Investing in renewable hydro, solar and wind power expands electricity while keeping emissions low, which is consistent with the Paris Agreement goal of limiting global warming. Coal, diesel and biomass burning increase greenhouse gas emissions.
